title: Automatic updates: system packages, AUR, npm globals and user tools
references: cr-0w logics/request/req_045_periodic_tool_update_watch.md (reads versions and changelogs only; installing belongs here)

needs: The owner updates the machine by hand and too often. Updates run on a schedule and the owner acts only when something needs them.
Covered: pacman, AUR (paru), npm globals (@grifhinz/logics-manager, Codex CLI), Claude Code, cdx, rtk, and the other user tools in ~/.local (uv tools, pipx venvs, codebase-memory-mcp).
Safety: Arch news is checked before any pacman -Syu, a snapshot exists before every system upgrade with a written rollback path, and a kernel upgrade never reboots the machine on its own.
One desktop notification when something needs the owner: news to read, system upgrade ready, reboot needed, a tool update failed. Nothing when all is fine.
crow (cr-0w req_045) reads installed versions and changelogs. Installing and upgrading live in this repo.
context: Today: ~/.local/bin/update-dev-tools.sh with update-dev-tools.timer (daily, Persistent, 30 min jitter) runs `cdx update all --yes` and `logics-manager update`. Neither file is in git.

`cdx update all` is an inventory plus a workstation plan: on 2026-11-09 it reported claude and rtk as UNKNOWN (latest unavailable) and codex as MISSING, and changed nothing. cdx itself (pipx venv cdx-manager, cdx 0.26.11) is not upgraded by that call.

Install methods found: logics-manager via npm -g with prefix ~/.local; Claude Code via its native installer (~/.local/share/claude/versions, built-in auto-updater); rtk 0.35.0 as a bare binary in ~/.local/bin (April 2026); cdx, code-review-graph, uv via pipx; ast-grep, graphify via uv tool; codebase-memory-mcp as a versioned dir; Codex CLI not installed.

System: paru (no yay), linux 7.2 only (no fallback kernel), snapper timeline + cleanup timers, snap-pac pre/post snapshots on every pacman transaction, grub-btrfs boot entries, pacman-contrib (checkupdates, pacdiff, paccache) installed. No system update check runs today.

Decision (this request): two tiers. User tools in ~/.local need no root and update unattended on a daily user timer. System packages (pacman + AUR) are never applied unattended: a daily no-root check (checkupdates, paru -Qua, Arch news) notifies, and the owner applies with one command (`sysup`) that runs the safety steps. Unattended -Syu breaks on news-flagged manual interventions and pacnew merges, and a kernel swap leaves the running kernel without modules until reboot.

Decision: cadence is systemd user timers with Persistent=true, so a missed run catches up at the next login or resume. No login hook. The system nudge fires at most once a day, and only when updates are older than a threshold (default 7 days), news is unread, or a security-flagged package is pending. The upgrade window is then weekly.

Decision: notifications go through notify-send to the shell's notification server, with an action that opens `sysup` in a kitty window. A bar widget for pending updates is a later archeotech-shell item, out of scope here.
Personal repo, private machine config (road_002). Scripts in scripts/, units in config/.config/systemd/user/, linked by install.sh.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: The user-tool updater and its timer are tracked in this repo, installed by install.sh, and update logics-manager, Codex CLI, Claude Code, cdx, rtk, uv tools and pipx venvs; one tool failing does not stop the others.
AC2: A daily no-root check records pending pacman and AUR updates and Arch news published since the last system upgrade, without changing the system.

AC3: `sysup` refuses to upgrade while news is unread until the owner acknowledges it, confirms a pre snapshot exists, runs paru -Syu, then reports pacnew/pacsave files, failed units and whether a reboot is needed. It never reboots.
AC4: The owner gets one notification per event that needs them (news, upgrade due, reboot needed, tool update failed), at most once a day per kind, and none when nothing is due.

AC5: A runbook covers the policy, the daily flow and rolling back a bad upgrade from a snapper snapshot via grub-btrfs. An ADR records the two-tier decision, and docs/TOOLS.md and docs/PACKAGES.md are updated.
AC6: Installed versions are written to a state file that crow (cr-0w req_045) can read without running any updater.

product.title: Automatic machine updates
product.overview: Scheduled, safe updates for the owner's Arch laptop: user tools update unattended, system packages are checked daily and applied with one guarded command, and the owner is notified only when something needs them.
goals: The owner stops checking for updates by hand.
No system upgrade runs without a news check and a snapshot to roll back to.
A kernel update never reboots the machine without the owner.
non_goals: Changelog reading and impact proposals (crow req_045).
A pending-updates bar widget in archeotech-shell (later shell item).

backlog_items.title: Update notifier and state file shared by all update jobs
problem: Every update job needs to tell the owner when something needs them, without repeating the same alert every run, and crow needs installed versions without running updaters.
scope_in: scripts/update-notify.sh: one entry point taking a kind (news, upgrade-due, reboot, tool-failed) and a message; rate limit per kind per day; action button that opens `sysup` in kitty for upgrade-due and news.
State dir ~/.local/state/archeotech-updates/: last notification per kind, versions.json (tool, installed version, method, last update time, last result), last system upgrade time.
Dry-run flag that prints the notification instead of sending it, for tests.
acceptance_criteria: AC4: A second call with the same kind on the same day sends nothing; a different kind sends.
AC6: versions.json is valid JSON with one entry per followed tool and is documented for crow.

backlog_items.title: Tracked user-tool updater: npm globals, Claude Code, Codex, cdx, rtk, uv, pipx
problem: The daily updater lives untracked in ~/.local/bin, does not upgrade cdx, rtk or Claude Code (cdx update all only lists them), and Codex CLI is not installed.
scope_in: Move update-dev-tools.sh and its service/timer into scripts/ and config/.config/systemd/user/, linked by install.sh; remove the untracked copies.

One updater per install method: npm -g (logics-manager, @openai/codex, installed when missing), Claude Code (`claude update`, with its auto-updater left on), cdx (pipx upgrade cdx-manager, then cdx update all for the workstation plan), rtk (GitHub release binary with checksum, or the method rtk documents), uv tool upgrade --all, pipx upgrade-all, codebase-memory-mcp (versioned dir switch).
Each tool runs alone with a timeout; failures call update-notify.sh tool-failed; results go to versions.json.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: After one run, every followed tool shows its latest version or a recorded failure reason; a forced failure in one tool leaves the others updated.
AC1: A fresh install.sh run installs the units and the timer is active.
AC6: versions.json lists each tool after the run.

backlog_items.title: Daily system update check with Arch news gate
problem: Nothing tells the owner when system updates are pending or when Arch news needs reading before an upgrade, so the owner checks by hand.
scope_in: scripts/update-check.sh (no root): checkupdates and paru -Qua counts and package lists, kernel/systemd/mesa/glibc flagged as notable, Arch news RSS items newer than the last system upgrade.
Writes pending.json in the state dir; unread news ids kept until `sysup --ack-news`.
Daily user timer (Persistent=true). Notifies upgrade-due when updates are older than the threshold (default 7 days) or news is unread.
Evaluate `checkupdates -d` to pre-download packages without touching the sync db.
acceptance_criteria: AC2: The check runs as the user, leaves /var/lib/pacman/sync untouched, and pending.json matches checkupdates output.
AC2: A news item newer than the last upgrade is listed as unread until acknowledged.
AC4: No notification when nothing is pending; one upgrade-due notification once the threshold passes.

backlog_items.title: sysup: guarded system upgrade command
problem: A system upgrade needs the same safety steps every time (news, snapshot, pacnew, reboot check) and the owner does them by memory or skips them.
scope_in: scripts/sysup.sh: shows unread news and refuses to continue until acknowledged; checks snap-pac is installed and snapper root config works; paru -Syu (owner enters the sudo password); after the upgrade, lists pacnew/pacsave (pacdiff -o), failed units, and AUR packages that need a rebuild.
Reboot check: running kernel modules dir missing or linux/systemd/glibc upgraded sets reboot-needed and calls update-notify.sh reboot. Never reboots.
paccache -rk2 after a successful upgrade; records last upgrade time in the state dir.
Records the snapper pre/post numbers for the rollback runbook.
acceptance_criteria: AC3: With an unread news item, sysup stops before paru and continues after acknowledgement.
AC3: After an upgrade, a snapper pre/post pair exists and the summary lists pacnew files and failed units.
AC3: A kernel upgrade ends with a reboot-needed notice and no reboot.

backlog_items.title: Update policy ADR, rollback runbook and docs
problem: The two-tier policy and the rollback path exist only in this request; the owner needs them written where they will look during a bad upgrade.
scope_in: ADR in logics/architecture/: two tiers (user tools unattended, system guarded), timer cadence, no unattended reboot, no unattended -Syu.
Runbook in docs/: daily flow, sysup, reading pending.json, rollback from a snapper snapshot via grub-btrfs boot entry then snapper rollback, recovering from a missing-modules state.
docs/TOOLS.md and docs/PACKAGES.md entries; note on a fallback kernel (linux-lts) as an owner decision.
acceptance_criteria: AC5: The ADR, the runbook and both docs exist and match the shipped scripts.
AC5: The rollback steps were tried once on a non-destructive snapshot listing (snapper list, grub-btrfs menu entries present).

orchestration_task.title: Orchestrate automatic updates
plan: Notifier and state file (everything else calls it).
Tracked user-tool updater (replaces the untracked daily job; quick win, no root).
Daily system check with Arch news gate (needs the notifier and state dir).
sysup guarded upgrade (consumes pending.json and the news acknowledgement from step 3).
ADR, rollback runbook and docs (written against the shipped scripts).
Validate each wave on the real machine with dry-run flags first; the first real sysup run is done by the owner.
